slug: 2026-03-31 Africa we have a data problem

facts.fact: The essay's Chad police row, scored 1, says the evidence suggests rural police stations are still predominantly paper-based, relying on traditional paper proces-verbaux at station level especially outside N'Djamena, with digitisation mainly at central level; no date is given, so the document's published date is used.

systems.owner: INTERPOL, EU-funded; managed through the Data Collection/Registration Center (DACORE/CREDOP)
systems.tiers: A centralised computerised database of police data (persons, offences, vehicles, documents) at the centre, which records and validates police data; access across agencies, regions and border posts is a longer-term plan dependent on infrastructure

note: An AI-assisted compilation by its own header, on the study's exclude_sources list; worded as inference ('evidence suggests'). It does not say stations enter reports or cases in SIPT, so the typology gives that system no class and no fact.
